title: Wandergrain Supply traveller-tee separations: turn four supplied 'Modern Wanderer' graphics into burnable press art -- vector spot masters for the flat designs, a holdable single-screen halftone for the continuous-tone one, and a four-page merged separation sell-sheet
grounding_note: Adapted from the real Freelancer.com brief 'Travel-Themed T-Shirt Design' (tees that 'capture the spirit of modern travellers' using 'universal icons (passports, coordinates, skylines)', delivered as 'layered vector files (AI or EPS) plus high-resolution PNGs with transparent backgrounds', 'keep text editable', and 'sized and pre-flighted for screen print or DTG'). The original from-scratch ART CREATION is out of connector scope, and the earlier version of this slot was killed for inverting the job into a report-only 'audit' whose every finding (halo detection, ink counting, LPI probing) required measurements the connector cannot make. REPOSITIONED to the real production work a screen-print shop actually does and the connector CAN do: the shop has received four finished 'Modern Wanderer' traveller graphics from its designer and must turn each into press-ready separation art the exposure room can burn -- honoring the brief's own 'transparent backgrounds', 'keep text editable / vector', and 'pre-flighted for screen print' requirements by PRODUCING clean vector spot masters, a printable halftone reseparation of the one continuous-tone design, and a laid-up separation sell-sheet. Fictional IP-clean brand (Wandergrain Supply Co., 'Modern Wanderer' line); no real trademarks, no location-specific or proprietary data; Freelancer.com is the grounding platform only, not the client.
one_line_ask: Take four supplied traveller-themed t-shirt graphics and prepare each as press-ready screen-print separation art: decide per design whether it is clean flat-spot art to vectorize into a crisp spot master, art whose background matte must be genuinely knocked out and whose near-duplicate inks must be merged to one screen before tracing, or continuous-tone/gradient art that cannot be spot-separated and must instead be reseparated into a single holdable halftone screen the manual press can hold -- then lay the four finished separations up as a one-page-per-design merged separation sell-sheet for the exposure room.
full_brief:
Wandergrain Supply Co., a small-batch apparel screen-print shop, is putting its new 'Modern Wanderer' traveller-tee line into production. The designer has handed over four finished graphics -- a passport-stamp badge, a latitude/longitude coordinate mark, a minimalist city skyline, and a compass-rose crest -- and we now need them turned into art the exposure room can actually burn screens from. We are NOT redesigning anything and NOT reshooting; we are preparing what we were given for the press.

Our shop rules, and the bar you must hit for each design: (1) Our manual press holds a limited number of screens, and every ink prints as its OWN solid screen -- so a design built from flat spot colors must come back as clean, crisp VECTOR separation art where each color is a solid holdable shape and any editable type stays sharp vector, not a soft raster. (2) A background has to be genuinely transparent -- if a design still carries a stray off-white matte or halo around it, that matte will burn as a phantom screen and print as a ghost box, so it must be truly knocked out to transparency before anything else, not just look transparent on screen. (3) If a design secretly uses several near-identical tones of what is really one ink, those must be collapsed to a SINGLE screen -- we are not burning three screens to print what should be one. (4) Some art is not spot-separable at all: anything built from smooth gradients, blends, or soft shadows is continuous tone, and a manual press cannot hold unlimited tones -- that art has to be reseparated into a single HALFTONE screen (one ink, dot pattern) that the mesh can actually hold, NOT left as a gradient and NOT force-traced into a tangle of vector shapes that will never register. Part of the job is deciding, per design, which of these situations you are looking at -- get the treatment wrong and the screen either won't burn or will print garbage, and you won't see it until it's on a shirt.

Deliverables: for each of the four graphics, the finished separation art in the correct form (vector spot master for the flat designs; a single-ink halftone separation for the continuous-tone one); plus a laid-up SEPARATION SELL-SHEET -- one page per design -- that drops each finished separation into our template alongside its garment placement, print size and ink-limit note from the production roster we're sending, exported press-ready so the exposure room and the client both have a single clean reference. Bind the roster copy verbatim -- don't rewrite our placements or sizes. Keep everything spot / halftone oriented for screen print -- no CMYK process conversion, no new artwork, no recoloring a design to a different palette.

inputs.name: tee_passport_stamp_badge.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat 2-color screen-print-style t-shirt graphic: a circular vintage passport-stamp badge reading 'MODERN WANDERER' around the rim with a small airplane and coordinate ticks in the center, rendered in exactly two flat spot inks (a warm cream and a faded travel-red), hard clean edges, no gradients, no soft shadows, on a fully transparent background, with generous transparent padding around the badge. Slight retro distress texture inside the shapes only. Crisp high-resolution flat art, about 4500 px on the long edge, suitable for tracing to clean vector.
inputs.realism_notes: The clean flat-spot control. Already transparent, two solid inks, hard edges -- the correct treatment is a straight prep-and-trace (crop to bounds, then vectorize) into a 2-color spot master; nothing to knock out, nothing to merge. Declared ~4500 px so any raster preview downscales (never upscales). gemini-3-pro-image for crisp legible badge type.

inputs.name: tee_coordinate_mark.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat minimalist screen-print t-shirt graphic: a latitude/longitude coordinate crosshair with the numbers '38.42 N / 27.14 W' (generic, not a real landmark) and a thin compass ring, drawn in what looks like a single dark ink but is actually a near-duplicate trio of very dark tones (a soft charcoal, a warm near-black, and a true black) that a novice would mistake for one color. Around the whole graphic sits a faint off-white 1-2 px halo / leftover matte from a sloppy export, so the background is NOT cleanly transparent. Hard flat shapes otherwise, about 4500 px on the long edge. Crisp flat raster.
inputs.realism_notes: The knock-out-and-merge case. Two real problems: a stray off-white halo that must be GENUINELY removed to transparency (else it burns as a phantom screen), and three near-duplicate dark tones that are really one ink and must be merged to a single screen before tracing. Correct chain: remove_background to transparency, mask the linework, collapse the near-dupe darks to one flat ink, crop to bounds, then vectorize into a single-ink master. Tracing it raw captures the halo rectangle -- the prep-before-trace trap.

inputs.name: tee_city_skyline.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A screen-print-style t-shirt graphic of a generic minimalist city skyline silhouette at dusk (no recognizable real landmark), rendered with a smooth multi-stop gradient sky (orange fading to deep purple) behind a black skyline, plus a soft drop shadow under the buildings -- clearly continuous-tone poster art, not flat spot art, with no hard color breaks. On a transparent background, about 4500 px on the long edge. Photoreal-ish blended tones.
inputs.realism_notes: The continuous-tone case -- the one that is NOT spot-separable. A gradient sky plus soft shadow is effectively unlimited tones; a manual press cannot hold that, and force-tracing it to vector yields an unusable tangle. Correct treatment: desaturate to a clean single-ink tonal ramp FIRST (so the black skyline stays solid and the sky becomes a printable tonal range), THEN apply a halftone so the continuous tone becomes a dot screen one ink can print. gpt-image-2 for the blended gradient/shadow look. ~4500 px so the halftone separation downscales to press size, never up.

inputs.name: tee_compass_rose_crest.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat 3-color screen-print t-shirt crest: a compass rose inside a shield banner reading 'WANDERGRAIN' with small registration crosshair marks and corner crop ticks placed just outside the artwork, rendered in three clean flat spot inks (navy, cream, mustard), hard edges, crisp editable-looking type, on a fully transparent background with generous transparent padding. Crisp flat vector-style art, about 4500 px on the long edge.
inputs.realism_notes: The second clean flat-spot case, but with registration crosshairs and crop ticks that MUST survive into the vector master so the shop can register the three screens. Correct treatment: crop to bounds (bounds include the reg marks, which are real content, not margin) then vectorize into a 3-color spot master. gemini-3-pro-image for legible type and clean flats.

inputs.name: wandergrain_sepsheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied, not model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign SINGLE-RECORD separation sell-sheet template (.indd/.idml, ~US Letter portrait at 300 DPI plus bleed) -- ONE design per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<design_name>>, <<tee_placement>>, <<print_size>>, <<ink_limit_note>>, a masthead area, and ONE image frame wired to an @-prefixed image-path merge column so the merge drops each finished separation preview into the sheet. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd with real <<fields>> plus a genuine @-image-path column, and produces ONE FILE PER ROW -- four roster rows => four single-record sheets. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd or a multi-record grid would not bind / cannot be produced by this tool.

inputs.name: wandergrain_production_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns design_name,tee_placement,print_size,ink_limit_note,@sep_preview holding exactly four rows, one per traveller graphic: 'Passport Stamp Badge' (front-left-chest, 4 in wide, 'manual press, max 4 screens'); 'Coordinate Mark' (back-yoke, 11 in wide, 'manual press, max 4 screens'); 'City Skyline' (full-back, 12 in wide, 'manual press, max 4 screens'); 'Compass Rose Crest' (front-center, 9 in wide, 'manual press, max 4 screens'). The @sep_preview column names the matching finished-separation preview file the agent produces (e.g. @passport_sep_preview.png). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<design_name>>,<<tee_placement>>,<<print_size>>,<<ink_limit_note>> and the @-image column.
inputs.realism_notes: Neutral production metadata only (placement, print size, ink-limit) -- it does NOT hand the solver the answers (which design needs which separation treatment is the agent's decision, not stated here). Headers match the authored .indd fields and the @-image column so the one-file-per-row merge binds copy AND the correct separation preview per design. Four rows => the merge must produce exactly four sheets.

outputs.name: passport_stamp_sep.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector spot-separation master of the passport-stamp badge: the two flat inks preserved as solid holdable shapes with crisp editable-type-quality edges, traced from the cropped-to-bounds transparent art. A genuine 2-screen spot master, not a silhouette and not a raster. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: coordinate_mark_sep.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector spot-separation master of the coordinate mark: the stray off-white halo GENUINELY knocked out to transparency (no phantom-screen matte) and the three near-duplicate dark tones collapsed to ONE flat ink before tracing, so the result is a single-screen master with no captured paper ground. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: compass_crest_sep.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector spot-separation master of the compass-rose crest: three flat inks preserved as solid shapes AND the registration crosshairs / corner crop ticks retained in the trace so the shop can register the three screens. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: city_skyline_halftone_sep.png
outputs.spec: A single-ink HALFTONE separation of the continuous-tone city skyline: the gradient sky and soft shadow first reduced to a clean one-ink tonal ramp (black skyline held solid), then converted to a visible halftone dot screen the manual mesh can hold -- a burnable one-screen separation, NOT a continuous-tone gradient and NOT a force-traced vector tangle. Downscaled to press size from the ~4500 px source (never upscaled). DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: Wandergrain_SepSheets_x4.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly four press-ready US Letter portrait separation sell-sheets -- ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 4) -- exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each sheet drops that design's finished separation preview into the image frame and binds <<design_name>>/<<tee_placement>>/<<print_size>>/<<ink_limit_note>> verbatim from the roster; ~300 DPI print quality. DELIVERABLE.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: tee_passport_stamp_badge.png, tee_coordinate_mark.png, tee_city_skyline.png, tee_compass_rose_crest.png, wandergrain_sepsheet_template.indd, wandergrain_production_roster.csv
connector_workflow.note: Load the four traveller graphics, the authored single-record .indd sell-sheet template and the production roster CSV into the working project in one batch so every downstream step has real asset references. Single upload -- plumbing, not the difficulty.

TRIAGE decision: the passport badge is already clean flat 2-color art on a transparent ground -- the correct treatment is a straight prep-and-trace, no knock-out and no ink-merge. Prep-before-trace step: trim the transparent padding to the badge's tight bounds so the vectorize traces only the artwork, not empty canvas.

Trace the prepared flat 2-color badge into a clean vector spot master -- each ink a solid holdable shape, type edges crisp. Feeding a raster (not a selection) so vectorize returns a color trace, not a black silhouette. DELIVERABLE passport_stamp_sep.svg.

Downscale the prepared transparent badge raster to a sell-sheet preview size (the @sep_preview cell the merge will bind for the Passport Stamp Badge row). Downscale-only from the ~4500 px source, never canvas-extend, never upscale.

TRIAGE decision: the coordinate mark carries a stray off-white halo, so the FIRST move is to genuinely knock the background/matte out to transparency via remove_background -- if that phantom matte survives it burns as a ghost screen. This is the correct knockout path (remove_background to transparency), NOT select->invert->fill (which would solid-fill and destroy the linework's interior gaps).

Semantically select the dark coordinate crosshair linework and numerals ('the dark coordinate crosshair, compass ring and number linework') so the ink-merge is confined to the artwork. Returns a maskURI -- a real-object selection, not a hue or coordinate pick.

Masked ink-merge: on the linework only, drop saturation to zero and push contrast/blacks so the three near-duplicate dark tones collapse to ONE flat solid ink -- reducing a hidden 3-screen mark to a single screen. image_apply_adjustments accepts a mask, so this stays off the transparent edges; a whole-image push is unnecessary and risks the anti-aliased fringe. This is the spot-count-reduction decision, reasoned by eye; the agent reports that it merged to one ink.

Prep-before-trace: trim the now-transparent, single-ink coordinate art to its tight bounds so vectorize traces only the mark. With the halo already removed and tones merged, the trace will be a clean single-ink master.

Trace the prepared coordinate mark into a clean single-ink vector master -- no captured off-white rectangle (halo gone), one screen (tones merged). Tracing the RAW file instead would have baked in the halo and split the one ink across near-dupe tones: the prep-before-trace trap this chain avoids. DELIVERABLE coordinate_mark_sep.svg.
Downscale the prepared single-ink coordinate raster to the sell-sheet preview size (the @sep_preview cell for the Coordinate Mark row). Downscale-only from source.

TRIAGE decision: the city skyline is continuous-tone (gradient sky + soft shadow), so it is NOT spot-separable and must NOT be vectorized. Dependent-step prep: FIRST reduce it to a clean single-ink tonal ramp -- drop saturation to zero and set contrast/whites/blacks so the black skyline stays solid and the gradient sky maps to a printable tonal range. Halftoning the full-COLOR gradient directly would produce color moire garbage; this desaturate-first step is the intermediate the halftone depends on.

Convert the single-ink tonal ramp into a halftone dot screen: continuous tone becomes variable-size dots a manual mesh can actually hold, so the whole skyline prints as ONE ink screen. This is the reseparation the continuous-tone art requires -- the agent-authored move that makes an unprintable gradient burnable. (image_apply_halftone has no LPI parameter; the agent applies it and reports that the skyline was reseparated to a one-ink halftone.)

Downscale the halftone separation to press size from the ~4500 px source (never upscale, never canvas-extend). This finished one-ink halftone is BOTH the skyline separation deliverable AND the @sep_preview the merge binds for the City Skyline row. DELIVERABLE city_skyline_halftone_sep.png.

TRIAGE decision: the compass-rose crest is clean flat 3-color art on transparency -- prep-and-trace, like the passport. Trim the transparent padding to the art's tight bounds; the registration crosshairs and crop ticks are dark CONTENT (not empty margin) so the bounds include them and they survive into the trace.

Trace the prepared crest into a clean 3-color vector spot master with the registration crosshairs / crop ticks preserved for screen registration. Raster in (not a selection) so the trace keeps the three flat inks as solid shapes. DELIVERABLE compass_crest_sep.svg.
Downscale the prepared crest raster to the sell-sheet preview size (the @sep_preview cell for the Compass Rose Crest row). Downscale-only from source.
Initialize an upload session for the four finished separation previews so the merge can resolve them by the roster's @sep_preview column.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @sep_preview column resolves to for each design's single-record sheet.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the four roster rows (design_name/tee_placement/print_size/ink_limit_note) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and drop that row's finished separation preview into the @-image frame, producing EXACTLY ONE merged sheet per row (four sheets). [T] requires the hand-authored template. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind the @image column) and a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind -- both avoided.

Export the merged single-record sheets to a press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF, one page per design. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 4; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed. This whole-document export is the only render of the merged set -- there is NO per-record pull-out of a single named sheet (document_render_layout exports the entire merged multi-page document, never one record as its own file). DELIVERABLE Wandergrain_SepSheets_x4.pdf.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into three heterogeneous per-design separation chains that converge on a merged sell-sheet. PASSPORT (clean flat spot): crop_to_bounds(2) -> vectorize(3, spot master) with a parallel downscale to a preview(4). COORDINATE (knock-out + ink-merge): remove_background(5, genuine halo knockout to transparency) -> select_by_prompt(6, linework mask) -> masked image_apply_adjustments(7, collapse near-dupe darks to one ink) -> crop_to_bounds(8) -> vectorize(9, single-ink master) with a preview downscale(10). SKYLINE (continuous-tone reseparation): image_apply_adjustments(11, desaturate to a one-ink tonal ramp -- the intermediate the halftone depends on) -> image_apply_halftone(12, dot screen) -> crop_and_resize(13, press-size halftone separation, also the preview). CREST (clean flat spot, reg marks kept): crop_to_bounds(14) -> vectorize(15, 3-color master) with a preview downscale(16). The four finished previews converge into the upload session(17) -> finalize(18) -> document_merge_data_layout(19), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one sheet per row (4 sheets). The merged set is exported once, as a whole, to the 4-page PDF(20) -- a single whole-document render, never a per-record pull-out of one named sheet. Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; nothing is composed or generated outside the chain. 20 calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon create-edit rebuilt from the killed report-only 'audit': 20 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three families (image_* prep/select/adjust/halftone/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single upload and the two merge-upload plumbing steps. Difficulty is DEPTH via a TRIAGE that the connector genuinely lets the agent get wrong: four superficially-similar traveller graphics need three DIFFERENT correct separation treatments, and the wrong one is invisible until the screen is burned -- vectorize the two clean flat-spot designs (passport 2-ink, crest 3-ink with reg marks preserved), but reseparate the continuous-tone skyline into a single halftone screen instead (force-tracing a gradient yields an unusable vector tangle; leaving it as a gradient is unprintable on a manual press), and knock out the coordinate mark's phantom halo AND merge its three near-duplicate darks to one screen BEFORE tracing (tracing it raw bakes in the matte rectangle and splits one ink across three screens). Each treatment is a dependent chain where a wrong intermediate breaks the downstream op: desaturating the skyline to one ink is a prerequisite for a clean halftone (halftoning the color gradient gives moire garbage); knocking out the halo is a prerequisite for a clean trace. The endpoint is a genuine authored-.indd one-file-per-row data merge (four rows -> four sheets, @-image column binding each finished separation, page=row and ~300 DPI acceptance) -- an owned designed artifact, not a findings file. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no compositing, no from-scratch art, no CMYK process split; image_vectorize is fed prepared rasters (not selections) so it returns real color separations; image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only from ~4500 px sources; deprecated adjust tools are replaced by image_apply_adjustments; convert_pdf_to_indd and document_merge_data_vector are explicitly avoided as merge paths.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, never a self-measurement): the four graphics require three divergent separation treatments and the agent trips the gate by mis-triaging -- vectorizing the continuous-tone skyline (garbage tangle of paths), halftoning or vectorizing the coordinate mark before its phantom halo is knocked out (a captured off-white rectangle that burns as a ghost screen) or without merging its three near-duplicate darks (three screens where one belongs), or halftoning the still-COLOR skyline gradient (moire); each failure is invisible on screen and only shows on the press, so the grader checks the delivered separations. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) triage of look-alike inputs to different correct treatments (flat-spot -> vector master; continuous-tone -> single halftone screen; halo+near-dupe -> knock-out-and-merge-then-trace); (2) constraint-reasoning around tool limits -- a gradient can only be held on a manual press as a one-ink halftone (not vector, not left continuous), a phantom matte must be removed via remove_background to transparency (not select->invert->fill), and a hidden multi-tone ink must be collapsed to one screen via a masked adjustment before tracing; (3) prep-before-trace discipline (crop-to-bounds, and for the coordinate mark knock-out + ink-merge) so vectorize traces only clean artwork. TRAP: the naive uniform path -- run image_vectorize on all four because 'they're all t-shirt graphics' -- looks right and fails twice (the skyline traces to an unusable tangle; the coordinate mark traces its halo and splits its one ink), and a second trap halftones the color skyline directly instead of desaturating to one ink first. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, no agent pixel-reading): passport SVG a clean 2-ink spot master and crest SVG a clean 3-ink master with registration marks retained; coordinate SVG a single-ink master with no captured halo ground; skyline delivered as a visible one-ink halftone dot screen (not a gradient, not a vector tangle) downscaled from source; the merged sell-sheet page-count == roster row-count == 4 with each finished separation placed and its copy bound verbatim at ~300 DPI; every raster output reachable by downscale from the ~4500 px declared sources. The agent reports the treatment it chose per design (vector spot / halo-knockout+ink-merge / halftone reseparation), an applied-decision log, not any measured value.
